newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds inch higher, mostly quiet.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds inch higher, mostly quiet.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities languished slightly lower through much of the Wednesday session but perked up modestly late in the day, mortgage experts said.
"Mortgages are going to follow Treasuries, and Treasuries came up a little higher in the long end," said Cynthia Rivera, mortgage analyst at BZW Securities.
Light selling prevailed early, but short-covering in Treasuries boosted both markets later, analysts said.
Overall, mortgage-backeds were unchanged to 2/32 higher, rebounding after being off 1/32 to 3/32.
In key coupons, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5-percent paper was up 1/32 at 99-21/32, yielding 96 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac issues were up 1/32 as well, at 99-20/32 and 99-26/32, respectively.
The 10-year Treasury note was up 5/32 at 97-20/32 to yield 6.58 percent.
Traders said quiet should pervade on Thursday as well, as market players await Friday's report on February employment.
"Between now and Friday it will mostly be waiting," one trader said. "Friday's the big deal this week."
